<role>
You write a one-page opportunity brief for a Keelwater product manager. Keelwater makes claims-handling software. You use only the facts and customer insights below.
</role>
<opportunity>
{
 "title": "Unscalable manual letter merge fixes",
 "problem_statement": "Users processing high volumes of claims must manually edit letter merge fields to correct errors. This workaround is inefficient and unsustainable for teams handling hundreds of claims weekly."
}
</opportunity>
<fact_sheet>
{
 "as_of": "2026-11-03",
 "accounts_n": 1,
 "mentions_n": 1,
 "routes_n": 1,
 "mentions_by_route": {
  "sales": 1
 },
 "arr_total_gbp": 1250000.0,
 "renewals_90d_n": 0,
 "accounts": [
  {
   "name": "Callowfield Auto Assurance",
   "arr_gbp": 1250000.0,
   "renewal_date": "2027-03-31",
   "mentions": 1
  }
 ]
}
</fact_sheet>
<insights>
[
 {
  "id": "ddd2160a67683c35",
  "quote": "That’s a workaround, but we’re handling 200+ claims a week—manual edits aren’t scalable.",
  "account": "Callowfield Auto Assurance",
  "route": "sales",
  "date": "2026-10-07T14:03:00Z"
 }
]
</insights>
<rules>
- Cite every insight you rely on as [i:INSIGHT_ID], using the id exactly as given. Cite at least three different insights when three or more are given, and cover every route that appears.
- Use these sections, in this order, as Markdown headings: "## Problem", "## Who is affected", "## Evidence", "## Why now".
- Every bullet under "Who is affected" and "Evidence" ends with a citation. Every sentence that contains a number or a date carries a citation.
- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Write counts as digits exactly as the fact sheet gives them ("5 accounts", never "five accounts"); never write "one customer" or "a single customer" unless the fact sheet count says 1 for that same thing.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word, character for character, from one insight cited in the same sentence. Never put quotation marks around a paraphrase, a fragment of your own wording or a phrase from the fact sheet; when unsure, paraphrase without quotation marks.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.
</rules>
<output>
JSON only: {"body_md": the brief as Markdown, "citations": the list of insight ids you cited}
</output>

{"body_md": "## Problem

Users processing high volumes of claims must manually edit letter merge fields to correct errors. This workaround is inefficient and unsustainable for teams handling hundreds of claims weekly.

## Who is affected

- Callowfield Auto Assurance, an account with £1250000.0 in ARR, is handling 200+ claims a week and reports that manual edits are not scalable [i:ddd2160a67683c35].

## Evidence

- The only insight in the fact sheet comes from the sales route: 1 mention across 1 account, with 1 route represented [i:ddd2160a67683c35].
- Callowfield Auto Assurance, with £1250000.0 in ARR and a renewal date of 2027-03-31, described the manual editing as a workaround that is not scalable at 200+ claims a week [i:ddd2160a67683c35].
- The fact sheet records 0 renewals in the next 90 days as of 2026-11-03 [i:ddd2160a67683c35].

## Why now

- The single mention is dated 2026-10-07 and arrived through the sales route, while the account's renewal date is 2027-03-31 and there are 0 renewals in the next 90 days as of 2026-11-03 [i:ddd2160a67683c35].
- No insight in the fact sheet points the other way; the evidence is limited to 1 account and 1 mention, so the scope of the problem beyond Callowfield Auto Assurance is not established [i:ddd2160a67683c35].
", "citations": ["ddd2160a67683c35"]}
